style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: A 200mm telephoto compression view of a vast data hall, captured as a split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast. On the left, standardized cloud server racks; on the right, high-density custom compute arrays. Constructed with galvanised steel, perforated metal, and glass. Sharp directional lighting from the right illuminates the aisles, casting deep industrial contrast. Steel blue, charcoal, and cobalt palette. Flat compressed perspective, stacked overlapping layers of structure with crystal-clear distance clarity, no people, no fog.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI, numbers, people
rationale: The story involves massive scale—30,000 merges a day and 600 PB of traffic—making a compressed telephoto view of a data hall the ideal choice. The split-screen duality perfectly captures the build-versus-buy contrast.

core_thesis: October 2026 drew the build-versus-buy line for developer tooling at the layer, not the licence, forcing engineering leaders to decide between vendor dependency and custom scale.
core_conflict: Standardized vendor cloud hosting versus the massive engineering cost of building and maintaining custom infrastructure.
